children: New Delhi, Oct. 18 -- Petrol and diesel prices today, October 18: Petrol and diesel prices remained steady across major cities today, with no revisions announced by oil marketing companies.
The cost of fuel varies across states and cities due to local taxes (Value Added Tax or VAT), freight charges, and other localised factors.
While global crude oil prices have fluctuated amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, domestic retail prices have remained unchanged.
Here is a look at the petrol and diesel prices in major metropolitan cities as of October 18:
New Delhi: Petrol is retailing at Rs.102.12 per litre, while diesel is priced at Rs.95.20 per litre. The national capital continues to have relatively lower fuel prices compared to other metros.
Mumbai: In the financial capital, petrol is priced at Rs.111.21 per litre, and diesel costs Rs.97.83 per litre.
Chennai: Residents in Chennai are paying Rs.107.76 per litre for petrol and Rs.99.55 per litre for diesel.
Kolkata: Petrol costs Rs.113.51 per litre, while diesel costs Rs.99.82 per litre.
Bengaluru: Petrol is priced at Rs.111.68 per litre, and diesel at Rs.99.56 per litre.
Hyderabad: Petrol costs Rs.116.15 per litre, while diesel costs Rs.104.23 per litre.

In India, public-sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) such as Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) revise fuel prices daily at 6:00 AM.
The pricing is based on a 15-day rolling average of international benchmark petrol and diesel prices, as well as the foreign exchange rate (rupee-dollar fluctuations).

US President Donald Trump wants to take a 60-day period to analyse what imposing sanctions on Russia and tariffs on other countries would mean for the global economy, said Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

"I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the US economy," Rubio said in response to a question on the waivers granted by Trump under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act or the Graham Act.

The US military has claimed that 97 per cent of vessels seeking to transit the Strait of Hormuz have passed through safely without being hit by Iranian projectiles, asserting that the strategic shipping route remains open despite attacks on commercial vessels.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) Spokesperson Navy Captain Tim Hawkins told Fox News Digital that coordinated naval protection efforts had helped thousands of commercial ships safely navigate the vital maritime corridor, even following the recent loss of a container ship in the regional waterway.
